requirementAssessments.evidence: moldea/moldea.yaml gives support only a runtimeAgent binding. Three warning-level unresolved entries separately cover post-middleware instruction, output, and tool-registration uncertainty, matching the non-empty middleware in src/support-agent.ts. Deterministic inspection and validation are valid.

step-support has only runtimeAgent and instructionLoader bindings. It has no canonical input, output, or tool relationship despite src/step-support-agent.ts using multiple response formats and state/context schemas and src/status-tools.ts defining a headless tool. Deterministic checks passed.

delegating-support retains its runtime-agent, instruction-loader, output-schema, and complete delegate-support function-tool bindings. No handoff, routing-target, or subagent declaration exists. src/delegation.ts still directly invokes stepSupportAgent, and runner hashes show all related source files were unchanged.

src/workflow-agent.mts still exports workflowSupportAgent as a direct StateGraph, with the same before/after hash. No workflow agent entry or canonical agent directory exists; the manifest registers only support, step-support, and delegating-support.

moldea/runtimes/langchain.md is the sole runtime guide and is referenced by both support and step-support. It concisely identifies direct createAgent targets, middleware uncertainty, unsupported step-support shapes, normal function-tool semantics, and the excluded StateGraph without asserting provider behavior. The patch inventory identifies this as the sole added guide.

The manifest contains focused warning entries for middleware instruction, output, and tool-registry uncertainty, each with an explicit resolution and related source paths. The shared guide separately characterizes multiple response formats, state/context schemas, and the headless client tool as unsupported canonical relationship shapes. Current hashes agree with the runner after-state and deterministic validation is valid.
